newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav PM sees Greece trip boosting trade.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav PM sees Greece trip boosting trade.

text.p: Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic visits Greece on Wednesday hoping to push next year's trade between the two states back to the $500 million they enjoyed before sanctions were imposed on Yugoslavia.

"The talks will focus on boosting bilateral economic cooperation, Yugoslavia's full reintegration into the international community and further development of regional and multilateral cooperation in the Balkans," Kontic told Tanjug news agency before his trip.

Sanctions imposed on the remains of federal Yugoslavia because of conflicts resulting from the break-up were ended last year, and trade with Greece reached some $250 million in 1996, half the pre-sanctions volume.

Kontic told Tanjug he will propose the opening of a mixed Yugoslav-Greek bank, seek a $100 million commodity credit and ask Athens to make it easier for Yugoslav businessmen to ship goods through the northern Greek port of Salonika.

Yugoslavia and Greece will sign accords to protect investments and avoid double taxation, and "If all these measures are agreed on, I may safely say the volume of trade next year will amount to $500 million," he said.
Yugoslavia will also urge liberalisation in movement of people, capital and goods between the two countries with a final aim of setting up a free trade zone among all the Balkan countries, he said.
